task_instance: Invoke /status-check (report once): build a single one-table report of all open work in the current session - running background jobs, durable trackers (todo list), and conversation items (handed to user / blocked on another session / CI / a bot), plus what finished since the last check. Created a realistic session-state sample in the work dir: two actual running background shell jobs with log files and pid files, a session todo tracker JSON, and a conversation-items JSON, then generated the report from that live state.
evidence: Work dir real2_work/r269. Set up sample session state: started two background shell jobs (build loop writing logs/build.log, test loop writing logs/tests.log) with pids saved in state/build.pid and state/tests.pid; wrote state/session_todos.json (5 todos: 2 in_progress, 2 blocked, 1 done) and state/conversation_items.json (delivered/waiting/done-since items). Wrote build_report.py (run with python3 -I) implementing the skill's gather order: (1) background work - checked each job alive via os.kill(pid,0) and read the latest log line without waiting on the job; (2) durable tracker - open todos; (3) conversation items + done-since. Output a single Markdown table of open items only, sorted needs-you-first then by actionability, with blocked-on-user items marked **needs you**, a Waiting-on column (you/CI/review bot/named session/named bot/a time), and a 'Done since last check: Release notes draft' line. Verified the report reflects real state: it correctly showed both background jobs as running with live pids (17303, 17304) and their most recent log lines (e.g. 'build step 6/10'), and listed 8 open items / 2 needing the user. Deliverable saved to report.md. No merge/rerun/edit/message actions were taken (skill is read-only), matching the skill's constraints. The optional '/status-check every N' timer branch would require this host's scheduled-prompt tools, which are out of scope for the one-shot core deliverable and were not exercised; the skill itself specifies a graceful degrade when such tools are absent. No network, no installs.
